title: Crystal Diffusion Variational Autoencoder for Periodic Material Generation
layout_note: An encoder on the left feeds a latent column, from which three rows branch right: a denoising row on top, a property-prediction row in the middle, and a generation row at the bottom that runs a short Langevin sequence; losses sit at the right ends of the top two rows.
grouping: Every material state is a dashed black square (unit cell). The three predicted quantities (composition, lattice, number of atoms) share one grey dashed rounded box joined by plus signs. Arrow colour separates the two phases: black for training, blue for generation, explained by a two-entry legend in the lower-left corner.
shapes_depth: Flat and glyph-like: atoms are solid discs in two colours (orange-red and teal) inside dashed squares; noised states shift and resize the discs; the intermediate Langevin states are small dashed squares. The latent is a narrow vertical column of grey cells. Function names are set in math under or over the arrows (encoder, decoder, aggregation MLP); losses are math symbols at the arrow ends. No 3-D, no shadows.
proposed_highlight: The networks are never boxes: they are function labels on arrows, while the drawn objects are the unit-cell states. Phase is the main visual distinction (black vs blue arrows).
lesson: Draw the crystal as one reusable glyph — a dashed unit-cell square with a few two-colour atom discs — and repeat it for every state (input, noised, denoised, random start, mid-Langevin, generated), colouring arrows black for training and blue for generation with a two-line legend.
notes: Venue read on the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2022'; venue_source: pdf).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: one vertical latent bar z in the middle feeds three rows that fan to the right: a noise-and-denoise row ending in L_Dec (top), a predicted-properties row ending in L_Agg (middle) and a Langevin-dynamics generation row (bottom)

relations.form: the latent z is a single tall cell strip from which three horizontal arrows leave, one per row ('Conditional' twice, 'Predict' once)
input crystal M at the left -> 'Encode' arrow labelled PGNN_Enc(M) -> z
every crystal is drawn as a dashed square unit cell holding red and teal atom discs; predicted composition, lattice and atom count are drawn as discs with 0.5, an empty dashed square and the number 4
the generation row shows a randomly initialised cell, two smaller intermediate cells under 'Langevin dynamics', and a final cell, joined by blue arrows
training and generation paths share the layout and are told apart by arrow colour (black training, blue generation) with a two-entry legend at bottom-left

channels.colour: arrow colour = phase (black = training, blue = generation, keyed); atom disc colour = element type
channels.shape: dashed squares = unit cells (crystal data), grey cell strip = latent
channels.line: solid = data flow; dashed black arrow = the noise-adding path; dashed outlines also draw unit cells and the grey predicted-properties box — dashes carry three meanings
channels.frame: a grey dashed box groups the predicted properties

quality.strengths: Crystals are drawn as toy unit cells with atoms at every stage, so noising, denoising and Langevin refinement act visibly on the structure; one latent bar feeding three rows shows the shared representation by geometry; phase is one colour channel with a legend.
quality.weaknesses: Dashed lines mean unit-cell border, noise path and property group at once; network names and formulas (PGNN_Dec(M̃|z), MLP_Agg(z), M̃ = (Ã, X̃, L)) are typeset on arrows; the noise path loops up and over from the input to the top row instead of starting at the row.

insights.structure: Input crystal at left -> encoder -> a vertical latent bar z in the middle, from which three rows run right: top a noise-and-denoise row ending in L_Dec, middle a grey dashed box of predicted properties ending in L_Agg, bottom a Langevin-dynamics generation row.
insights.data: Every material is a dashed black square unit cell holding red and teal atom discs; the latent is a vertical strip of grey cells; the predicted composition, lattice and number of atoms are drawn as atom discs with 0.5, an empty dashed square and the number 4 joined by plus signs.
insights.emphasis: Arrow colour separates the two phases (black training, blue generation) explained by a two-entry legend; the generation row shows shrinking intermediate cells to convey iterative Langevin refinement.
insights.flow: Left to right from input to z, then fanning right into three parallel rows; a dashed 'Add noises' line loops over the top from the input to the noisy cell; a blue 'Rand. init.' arrow drops from the property box into the generation row.
insights.avoid: The legend is squeezed directly under the input cell and the long dashed noise arrow over the top crosses above everything; the rows have no enclosure, so training and generation rows are separated only by arrow colour.

arrangement.units: three unenclosed horizontal rows (denoising training, property prediction, generation) branching from one latent; only the property row has a grey dashed rounded box
arrangement.inputs_as: a dashed unit-cell square with coloured atoms labelled M = (A, X, L)
arrangement.losses_at: right end of the top two rows (L_Dec, L_Agg)
arrangement.shared: the latent z feeds all three rows; PGNN_Dec(M|z) appears in both the training and generation rows
